- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +0.8–1.2% bias to first 7 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model exhibits erratic behavior; smooth forecast by averaging 3-day moving average of prior 30d forecast.
- If true price exceeds model forecast by >3% for 2+ consecutive days, model is lagging; adjust next forecast up by 1–1.5% to catch momentum.
- For sentiment >0.7 and price >70, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overbought bias.
